short_title: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology

title: The Hovey–Strickland and Chai conjectures
summary: Proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture for Lubin–Tate deformation rings over finite residue fields, at every prime and positive height n. Through the implication of Barthel–Heard–Naumann, this proves the Hovey–Strickland conjecture: dualizable $`K(n)`$-local spectra have exactly $`n+2`$ thick tensor ideals, and their Balmer spectrum is a chain of $`n+1`$ points.
subject: Topology
short_title: Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture

title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
summary: Proves the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for ∞-groupoids associated with every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention: these algebraic objects recover the homotopy theory of spaces.
subject: Topology
short_title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis

title: Finite generation for the $`K(n)`$-local sphere
summary: Answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland: every homotopy group of the $`K(n)`$-local sphere is a finitely generated ℤp-module, for every prime, positive height and integer degree. The same conclusion holds after $`K(n)`$-localizing any finite p-local spectrum.
subject: Topology
short_title: Finite generation for the $K(n)$-local sphere

title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
summary: Determines the optimal chromatic loss from geometric H-fixed points to geometric G-fixed points for every subgroup H of a finite p-group G. At every nonnegative height, the loss equals the shortest subnormal-chain length from H to G with cyclic quotients. Each quotient counts once regardless of order, and finite spectra witness sharpness.
subject: Topology
short_title: The chromatic Smith fixed-point problem for finite $p$-groups

title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
summary: Proves that the L2-Betti numbers of the universal cover of every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold vanish outside degree two. More generally, the same conclusion holds for every finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex of formal dimension four, proving the four-dimensional Singer conjecture in this wider class.
subject: Topology
short_title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture

title: Curtis’s conjecture
summary: Proves Curtis’s conjecture: the positive-degree mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the images of the Hopf-invariant-one classes η, ν, σ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist.
subject: Topology
short_title: Curtis’s conjecture

title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions
summary: Resolves the Ara–Maltsiniotis conjecture: for every n ≥ 1 and n = ω, small strict globular n-categories admit proper combinatorial Thomason model structures Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. Thus strict higher categories model the homotopy theory of spaces in every stated dimension.
subject: Topology
short_title: Thomason model structures in every strict higher dimension

title: Chromatic splitting: filtrations and counterexamples
summary: Disproves strong chromatic splitting at height three for primes p ≥ 5, and weak splitting for the derived p-completed sphere at heights p (p ≥ 5) and $`p+1`$ (p ≥ 7). Nevertheless, for n ≥ 1 and $`p\gt n+1`$, the overlap $`L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge`$ admits a $`2^n`$-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces. At height three and prime three, even finite assembly from such pieces fails in the category of $`E(2)`$-local modules over the derived completed sphere.
subject: Topology
short_title: Chromatic splitting: counterexamples and filtrations

title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
summary: Refutes the Hahn–Wilson conjecture at chromatic height two. For every sufficiently large prime p, constructs a connective p-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two that cannot be built from completed $`\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle`$ by finitely many sums, shifts, cones and retracts. The examples nevertheless satisfy the finite and telescopic localization comparisons.
subject: Topology
short_title: Counterexamples to the Hahn--Wilson conjecture at height two

title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
summary: Constructs closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group. This disproves even the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.
subject: Topology
short_title: A four-dimensional counterexample to Borel rigidity

title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) problem
summary: Constructs a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex whose universal cover has no integral homology above degree two and whose third cohomology vanishes for every local coefficient module, but which has no finite two-dimensional homotopy model. This disproves Wall's finite D(2) conjecture; the example has infinite fundamental group.
subject: Topology
short_title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) conjecture

title: Tingley’s sphere-isometry problem
summary: Resolves Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces. No dimension restriction is imposed, so the metric geometry of the unit sphere determines the Banach space up to linear isometry.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Tingley's sphere-isometry problem

title: Independence of the separable quotient problem
summary: Establishes, relative to the consistency of a measurable cardinal, that the separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC. The assertion that every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient can hold for all real and complex Banach spaces, whereas the continuum hypothesis yields counterexamples over both fields.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Relative independence of the separable quotient problem

title: Lipschitz equivalent Banach spaces need not be linearly isomorphic
summary: Constructs separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic, resolving the separable Lipschitz-isomorphism problem negatively. Thus even the complete metric structure up to bi-Lipschitz equivalence does not determine a separable Banach space's linear isomorphism class.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Lipschitz equivalence without linear isomorphism

title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture
summary: Resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture: for every bounded operator A on a complex Hilbert space and every finite matrix-valued polynomial P, one has $`\lVert P[A]\rVert\le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\lVert P(z)\rVert`$, where $`W(A)`$ is the numerical range. The constant 2 is sharp, independent of the matrix size, and valid in infinite dimensions.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture

title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property
summary: Resolves the cotype–cotype conjecture for real Banach spaces with the approximation property. Such a nonzero space is K-convex if and only if both it and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype, with possibly different exponents. Equivalently, these cotype assumptions force nontrivial Rademacher type.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: The cotype--cotype conjecture under the approximation property

title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
summary: Proves that every real Banach space with Markov type p for some p > 1 admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm, answering Naor's renorming question. Together with the known converse, this characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity

title: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive Banach spaces
summary: Resolves Kirk's reflexive-space fixed-point problem: every nonexpansive selfmap of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. The result uses the original norm, without assuming uniform convexity.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Fixed points of nonexpansive maps in reflexive Banach spaces

title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
summary: Disproves Pietsch's dimension-free duality conjecture for metric entropy. Origin-symmetric convex bodies violate every proposed choice of universal constants in the conjectured comparison between covering numbers and those of the polar bodies, even when the covering body is a cube.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: A counterexample to Pietsch's metric-entropy duality conjecture

title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces
summary: Constructs a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free Banach space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively. Finite-rank operators approximate the identity on every compact set, but their norms cannot share a finite bound.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: A negative answer to Kalton's Lipschitz-free approximation question

title: Reflexive midpoint convexity and diamond distortion
summary: Constructs a real reflexive Banach space with an asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm but no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, extending Baudier's separation to reflexive spaces. In the same space, depth-k countably branching diamonds require distortion at least $`\sqrt{1+k/12}`$, so midpoint uniform convexity does not force uniformly bounded diamond distortion even under reflexivity.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity without asymptotically uniformly convex renorming

title: Metric Markov cotype of ℓ1 and Hilbert-space Lipschitz extension
summary: Proves that real ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype two, answering Mendel and Naor's question. Consequently, every Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset of a real Hilbert space into ℓ1 extends to the whole space with a universal multiplicative loss in its Lipschitz constant, resolving Ball's extension problem for this target.
subject: Functional analysis
short_title: Metric Markov cotype two for $\ell_1$

title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into ℝ4
summary: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ4, resolving the closed-surface form of the four-dimensional isometric-immersion problem. This includes nonorientable surfaces and metrics of arbitrary Gaussian curvature.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into $\mathbb R^4$

title: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in ℝ3
summary: Constructs a smooth positive-definite metric on $`(-1,1)^2`$ for which no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ3. This answers the unrestricted smooth local isometric realization problem for surfaces negatively, even after shrinking the neighborhood.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: A smooth surface metric with no local immersion in $\mathbb R^3$

title: Gromov’s integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
summary: Proves $`\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert`$ for every closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 3, and every smooth metric, with $`a_n\gt 0`$ depending only on dimension. Here $`\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}`$ and $`\lVert M\rVert`$ is real simplicial volume. Also proves rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov–Lawson conjecture; every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Gromov's integral scalar-curvature inequality

title: Spectral scalar curvature, Urysohn width, and macroscopic dimension
summary: Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold, n ≥ 3, satisfying $`-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1`$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $`n-2`$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only by n in the original metric. This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $`n-2`$ for every n ≥ 2.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Spectral scalar curvature and codimension-two width

title: Sharp Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and rigidity
summary: Proves generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball. Bounded positive-volume equality regions for κ = 0 are Euclidean balls. Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral n-cycles, n ≥ 2, in arbitrary proper CAT$`(0)`$ spaces.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetry and CAT$(0)$ fillings

title: Yau's uniformization conjecture
summary: Proves Yau's uniformization conjecture: every complete connected noncompact Kähler manifold with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to ℂn.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Yau's uniformization conjecture

title: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture
summary: Proves Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture for closed connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least three with strictly negative sectional curvature: normalized Liouville measure maximizes entropy for the geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture

title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture
summary: Disproves the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture. For some sufficiently large even N, constructs a closed exact embedded Lagrangian in $`T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})`$ that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to its zero section.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture

title: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture
summary: Proves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture in a cohomology-preserving form. Every positive triple of smooth closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold, normalized by $`\int\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}`$, deforms through positive closed triples to a hyperkähler triple while preserving all three cohomology classes. Any positive triple can first be normalized by a constant linear change.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture

title: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture
summary: Proves Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture: every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold that is tamed by a symplectic form admits a compatible symplectic form. The almost complex structure stays fixed; the form's cohomology class may change.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture

title: Symplectic ball packing in higher dimensions
summary: Resolves the Siegel–Yao conjecture for arbitrary capacities in every dimension $`2n\ge6`$. Finitely many closed symplectic balls of capacities $`R_1,\ldots,R_k`$ embed disjointly into an open ball of capacity R exactly when $`\sum_iR_i^n\lt R^n`$ and $`R_i+R_j\lt R`$ for every distinct pair i, j.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Sharp symplectic ball-packing criteria in higher dimensions

title: The metric Blaschke conjecture
summary: Proves the metric Blaschke conjecture: every closed connected Riemannian manifold of positive dimension whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is, up to scaling, a standard compact rank-one symmetric space.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: The metric Blaschke conjecture

title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on Riemannian spheres and closed three-manifolds
summary: Proves that every smooth Riemannian metric on Sn, n ≥ 2, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The same conclusion holds on every closed manifold admitting a finite smooth spherical cover and on every closed three-manifold, without orientability or nondegeneracy restrictions.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on spheres and three-manifolds

title: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds
summary: Proves that every stationary integral m-varifold in a Euclidean open set has singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $`m-1`$, a sharp bound in every positive dimension and codimension. On round spheres, the family also proves almost-everywhere regularity: the singular set has zero m-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds

title: Counterexamples to stable-Morse and strong Arnold fixed-point bounds
summary: Disproves stable-Morse lower bounds for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points: on simply connected closed Kähler manifolds of real dimension 22, the deficit below the stable Morse number is unbounded. A separate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold has exactly three fixed points, fewer than the four critical points required of every smooth function.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Counterexamples to strong forms of Arnold's fixed-point conjecture

title: Nonnegative-curvature Einstein classification and an L2 topological gap
summary: Classifies closed connected Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative sectional curvature: up to scaling, their universal Riemannian covers are the round S4, Fubini–Study $`\mathbb{CP}^2`$, or a product of equal round two-spheres. A closed simply connected nonnegatively curved four-manifold is diffeomorphic to one of these whenever the scale-invariant L2 norm of its trace-free Ricci curvature lies below a universal positive constant.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Nonnegatively curved Einstein four-manifolds and a topological gap

title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture
summary: Proves the Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres. For every m ≥ 2, a closed connected minimal immersion into the unit sphere $`S^{m+1}`$ with non-totally-geodesic image has volume at least that of the smallest minimal Clifford product, counting covering multiplicity.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: The Solomon--Yau least-volume conjecture

title: Yau’s nodal bounds: surfaces and higher dimensions
summary: Proves the sharp $`C\sqrt\lambda`$ upper bound for nodal length on every fixed smooth closed surface, completing Yau's conjecture there. The upper bound fails for fixed smooth metrics in dimensions three and four, including metrics on S3 arbitrarily close to round. In dimension five, nodal measure can grow faster than $`\lambda^{1/2+\varepsilon_0}`$ for some fixed $`\varepsilon_0\gt 0`$, ruling out even arbitrarily small power losses.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Yau's nodal conjecture: surfaces and counterexamples

title: Scalar curvature and finite-time Ricci-flow singularities
summary: Proves that a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold extends past any finite time at which scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded. A higher-dimensional counterexample has bounded scalar curvature but unbounded full curvature at its finite maximal time, disproving the unrestricted scalar-curvature extension conjecture.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Scalar curvature detects four-dimensional Ricci-flow singularities

title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow
summary: Disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture for Calabi flow by constructing a smooth $`U(10)`$-invariant Kähler metric on $`\mathbb{CP}^{10}`$ whose flow develops a finite-time singularity. The metric lies in the Fubini–Study class, so the failure occurs even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Finite-time singularity of Calabi flow

title: Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample
summary: Proves that every smooth locally uniformly convex affine-maximal graph of dimension three through nine, complete for its induced Euclidean metric, is an elliptic paraboloid. A smooth entire nonquadratic example in dimension ten makes this range sharp. In dimensions three through nine, the paraboloid classification also holds for connected open locally uniformly convex affine-maximal hypersurfaces complete for the affine Berwald–Blaschke metric.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: The sharp dimension threshold for affine Bernstein rigidity

title: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus
summary: Determines the isoperimetric profile of the unit cubic flat three-torus and classifies every finite-perimeter minimizer: balls, circular tubes around shortest closed geodesics, coordinate slabs, and their complements. The transition volumes are $`4\pi/81`$ and $`1/\pi`$, with exactly the adjacent two types minimizing at each transition.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Isoperimetric regions in the cubic three-torus

title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity
summary: Proves the first-singular-time case of tangent-flow uniqueness for smooth compact connected embedded surfaces without boundary in ℝ3. At every singular point, all fixed-center backward tangent flows agree as area measures at every negative time in the original ambient coordinates, without mean-convexity or a prescribed tangent model.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity

title: Gigli’s characterization of Alexandrov curvature
summary: Proves Gigli's conjecture: in every integer dimension n ≥ 2, Alexandrov curvature at least κ is characterized by the full-support $`\mathop{\mathrm{RCD}}\nolimits ((n-1)\kappa,n)`$ condition with reference measure $`\mathcal H^n`$ and distributional sectional curvature at least κ in the original global test classes. The RCD condition is unreduced.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Gigli's characterization of Alexandrov curvature

title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point
summary: Proves that every regular point of a noncollapsed $`\mathop{\mathrm{RCD}}\nolimits (K,n)`$ space, for K ∈ ℝ and integer n ≥ 2, has an open neighborhood bi-Lipschitz to an open subset of ℝn. Regularity requires all pointed tangents to be Euclidean, the reference measure is exactly $`\mathcal H^n`$, and the chart compares ambient distances with a point-dependent finite constant.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point

title: A three-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature
summary: Constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. This answers negatively, already in dimension three, whether the first metric-existence property implies the second.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: A three-manifold with no conjugate points and no nonpositively curved metric

title: Negative Kähler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates
summary: Constructs a contractible domain in ℂ3 with a complete negatively pinched Kähler metric but no bounded holomorphic coordinates, disproving bounded-domain uniformization in this setting. A higher-dimensional example has sectional curvature at most −1 and only constant bounded holomorphic functions; its curvature is not bounded below.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Negative K\"ahler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates

title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport
summary: On every closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang curvature, all tangent injectivity domains are convex, resolving Villani’s conjecture in this setting. For squared-distance transport between measurable probability densities bounded above and away from zero, the optimal map and its inverse are Hölder continuous.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Villani’s convexity conjecture and regular optimal transport

title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
summary: Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 has at least $`(k+2)^2`$ independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count $`(k+1)^2`$. The metric may depend on k.
subject: Differential geometry
short_title: Counterexamples to Yau's harmonic dimension bound

title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
summary: Proves large-data global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional, one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. Smooth admissible initial data may be arbitrary provided the particle density is compactly supported and the electromagnetic fields have finite energy and bounded derivatives of every order; the solution remains smooth on every finite time interval.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell

title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
summary: Constructs two distinct global entropy solutions of the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation from the same nonnegative initial density, with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy and absolute entropy. Both are strongly continuous in L1 and satisfy exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation

title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan
summary: Derives the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from three-dimensional grand-canonical Newtonian gases throughout every regular kinetic interval with uniform Gaussian decay. Stable finite-range radial potentials may have attractive wells and a singular repulsive core; initial pair exclusion and spatially summable Gaussian density and gradient bounds are assumed. A companion gives finite-dimensional hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations, centered at the exact microscopic expectation and governed by the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan

title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch
summary: Zero-frequency measurements on any nonempty open boundary patch determine a smooth metric and smooth unitary connection on a trivial Hermitian rank-two bundle over a compact connected manifold of dimension at least three, up to diffeomorphism and gauge fixed on that patch. Inputs and observations use the same patch. In contrast, distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a three-dimensional ball can have identical full-boundary data.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch

title: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture and local weak-L4 gradient bounds
summary: Resolves the interior regularity conjecture for reduced absolute planar Mumford–Shah minimizers with bounded fidelity data. Locally, the closed discontinuity set is a $`C^{1,\alpha}`$ arc, a regular crack tip, or three arcs meeting at $`120^\circ`$; only finitely many global connected components meet any compact interior region.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: The planar Mumford--Shah regularity conjecture

title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
summary: Establishes seven as the first dimension admitting a nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy. Consequently, minimizing free boundaries are smooth through dimension six, and their singular sets have dimension at most $`n-7`$ in higher dimensions.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem

title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem
summary: Resolves the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem: every $`W^{1,p}`$ homeomorphism between arbitrary bounded domains in ℝ3, for $`1\le p\lt \infty`$, is a strong $`W^{1,p}`$ limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: The three-dimensional Ball--Evans approximation problem

title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains
summary: Proves a strict form of Burdzy's simply connected hot spots conjecture. On every smooth bounded simply connected planar domain, each nonzero eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has no interior critical point, so all global extrema lie on the boundary. Eigenvalue multiplicity is allowed.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains

title: The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures
summary: Resolves the subcritical Lane–Emden conjecture and its weighted Hénon extension. For n ≥ 2, $`p,q\gt 0`$ and real A, B, the system $`-\Delta u=|x|^A v^p`$, $`-\Delta v=|x|^B u^q`$ has no positive entire solution when $`(n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1)\gt n-2`$, with solutions continuous at the origin and classical elsewhere. No symmetry or growth assumption is needed. Known radial existence gives the exact existence criterion for n ≥ 3 and $`A,B\gt -2`$.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: The subcritical Lane--Emden and H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjectures

title: Stable blowup for the defocusing Schrödinger equation
summary: For a sufficiently large odd nonlinearity power, constructs a nonempty open set of initial data in $`H^k(\mathbb T^{12})`$, with k > 8, whose solutions of the scalar defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation blow up in finite time. Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Stable blowup for a defocusing Schr\"odinger equation

title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity
summary: Proves that full static boundary displacement-to-traction data determine both smooth real Lamé moduli on every bounded connected smooth domain in ℝ3, provided μ > 0 and $`3\lambda+2\mu\gt 0`$ on the closure. Neither analyticity, proximity to constant coefficients nor prior knowledge near the boundary is required.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity

title: Nonattainment of the three-marginal Coulomb Monge problem
summary: An optimal three-particle Coulomb configuration need not be a deterministic function of the first particle, even for smooth identical spatial densities. The Monge and Kantorovich infima agree, but the Monge infimum is not attained. The same phenomenon occurs for every inverse-power Riesz exponent in each dimension at least two, with a suitable density in each case.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Nonattainment in three-marginal Coulomb transport

title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps
summary: For uniform source measure ρ on a compact convex body with interior in dimension at least two, quadratic optimal transport maps satisfy $`\|T_\mu-T_\nu\|_{L^2(\rho)}\le C W_2(\mu,\nu)^{1/3}`$ uniformly over targets in a fixed compact set. The exponent is sharp, even for three-atom targets, disproving Letrouit's conjectured square-root bound.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Sharp one-third stability of optimal transport maps

title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
summary: Proves De Giorgi's conjecture at its sharp dimension-eight endpoint: every entire C2 solution $`u:\mathbb R^8\to(-1,1)`$ of $`\Delta u=u^3-u`$ that is strictly increasing in one direction depends on only one linear coordinate. A stronger theorem classifies all stable entire solutions $`v:\mathbb R^7\to[-1,1]`$ as constant wells or planar transitions, without an energy-growth assumption.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight

title: Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows
summary: Constructs viscous incompressible flows starting from rest on a fixed flat three-dimensional domain that perform universal computation under smooth external forcing. A terminating compiler turns a Turing machine and input into a finite program for the force, so a designated particle reaches a fixed region exactly when the machine halts. The viscosity is fixed, positive and computable.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Universal computation in forced Navier--Stokes flows

title: Interior $`C^{1,\alpha}`$ regularity for infinity-harmonic functions
summary: Proves uniform interior $`C^{1,\alpha_d}`$ regularity for bounded infinity-harmonic functions in every dimension d ≥ 3, for a positive exponent depending only on dimension. The gradient's supremum norm and Hölder seminorm on the half unit ball are bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times the oscillation on the unit ball. The exponent is not explicit.
subject: Partial differential equations
short_title: Interior $C^{1,\alpha
